summary: Cleared every outstanding security advisory in the web interface dependencies — 34 of them across all five apps and the product website, fourteen rated high. Most were build-time tooling rather than anything a user's browser ever runs, but a few (the routing library, an image-processing library, an HTTP client) do end up in shipped code, and leaving known advisories open is not a position worth defending. Three libraries needed a major version step and one was simply deleted: the door-controller app carried a routing library it never once imported, and the best fix for a vulnerable dependency is not upgrading it. Nothing about how any app looks or behaves changes.
compatibility: No configuration changes, nothing to migrate, and no change to any feature. The one thing worth recording is how it was checked, because a dependency update changes the compiled web interface and a broken one looks exactly like a working one from the outside: every app was rebuilt and then loaded in a real browser, and the two flagship apps had their full on-screen checks re-run against the final build. Also fixed while doing this: the fleet's own tooling now has a way to prove an app's web interface still loads without needing a database behind it, which is what the three smaller apps previously had no way to show. The door-controller app is fixed too but has no release channel yet, so it is not listed above.
